target_customer: Consumers wanting premium electric skateboards and later scooters for last mile commuting
problem: Existing electric skateboards were heavy, slow or poorly designed, and short trips lacked a fun lightweight vehicle.

founders.name: Sanjay Dastoor
founders.background_notes: Named a founder by Wikipedia, not on the YC page.

founders.name: John Ulmen
founders.background_notes: Founder and CTO per YC page.

exit.reason: Layoffs of most staff on March 4, 2020, then asset sales. Company cited US China trade war pressure.

technical_complexity.rationale: Custom hardware, motors, batteries and firmware needed for a small team, plus manufacturing.

defensibility.rationale: Industrial design and patents, five of which went to Lime, but later Chinese competitors copied features.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: No incumbent acquired it as a going concern. Lime bought patents and Boosted USA bought inventory in 2020.

market_need_then: Electric skateboards existed in niche form and a 2012 Kickstarter drew 467 thousand dollars from 1,110 backers, showing enthusiast demand.

branding.domain_note: Used boostedboards.com, matching the original name Boosted Boards.

identity.logo: Three sets of two curved lines forming a triangle shape
identity.visual_style: Orange wordmark in capitals on black decks

branding.brand_signature: Orange Boosted wordmark and cult riding community

rebrands.why: Broadened from skateboards to scooters, reason inferred from product line and not stated by a source.

branding.community_and_virality: Riding groups, Reddit threads and YouTube channels per a summary in search results.

brand_strength.rationale: Cult status among riders and premium reputation, though financial trouble and warranty complaints followed the shutdown.

outcome_analysis: Boosted launched a Kickstarter board in 2012, built a cult following and raised 60 million dollars in December 2018 for global expansion and new products. After moving production to China, the company cited US China trade war tariffs and financial pressure, and slidebean and press accounts also point to the costly Rev scooter and rising Chinese competition. It laid off most staff in March 2020 and sold its patents to Lime and its inventory to Boosted USA in April 2020.
notes: YC lists status Acquired but sources show a shutdown with asset sales, so the exit is recorded as acquisition of assets. Series A with StartX and Bay Meadows had undisclosed amount, and a 10.7 million dollar figure on Wellfound is unverified. Search found no 2012 dated competitor coverage so the list is empty. boostedboards.com could not be read (too many redirects). Founder education and employers not found. The Series B lead investor is disputed across sources. No formal bankruptcy filing was confirmed.
